writeup: TIC 78199363 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 15.945481 days, detected in TESS photometry with a signal-to-noise ratio of 510.7. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 21.83 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal at the target's location with a peak signal-to-noise of 23.2, though the centroid offset of 5.5 arcsec warrants note. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a significant data quality flag indicates that successive eclipses differ notably in depth, suggesting the true period is double the initial detection - a pattern consistent with how the automated pipeline sometimes underestimates periods in such cases. This candidate merits further investigation to clarify its nature.
